files.content: # Briefing board — Style Prompt > One real whiteboard, filmed: warm enamel with window light and the ghosts of erased marker, an aluminium frame and a tray. Marker ink draws itself in three colours with fixed meanings (graphite for names and rules, blue for measurement, red only for the verdict), cut-out photographs of the real thing are lowered onto the board and pinned with glossy magnets, tags swing on their magnets, and a pitted stamp lands with a thud. The camera rides the lines from fact to fact, close and off-centre, pushes in slowly with a slight tilt when the test is about to fail, and only at the end pulls back to show the whole board as one poster. A frosted subtitle strip carries the voice. ## 1. Essence, and what it is not 1. **A physical board in a room.** Enamel with a soft window falloff, mottling and faint ghosts of earlier writing, a sliding diagonal reflection, a lens vignette; the aluminium frame and the marker tray are seen only in the final pull-back. 2. **Real things on it.** The subject is a cut-out photograph (or a photo-real painting of it) lying a few millimetres above the board: clean edge, one shared grade, a soft shadow from one window. It is evidence, measured against drawn limits. 3. **Ink that means something.** Graphite names and counts, blue measures (limits, dimension lines with open arrowheads), red decides (a stamp, the rule written after it). A rejected idea is erased to a blurred ghost, never deleted. 4. **One continuous wall.** No pages and no cuts: every beat is a crop of the same board, reached by moving the camera along a line. 5. **The whole wall, once.** Design the final board as a poster first; every earlier shot shows at most about 60 % of its width and never both side edges. Not a whiteboard-animation explainer (a hand drawing flat line art on a white page): the board is a filmed object and the subject is a photograph. Not a data dashboard: comparisons are dimension lines in real units beside real things, and counts are magnets. Not a stage talk: no headers, centred bullets or page turns. ## 2. Materials & rendering - **Enamel (z 0):** `--latar` with a radial window falloff toward `--latar-2` (upper left), 200 faint blotches, a dozen ghost lines of joined small writing at 4-8 % opacity, eraser wipes in `--latar-2`. Painted once into a quarter-size canvas and shown as an ``, so it is soft when the camera is close. - **Ink:** strokes 10-12 px on a 3900 × 2200 board at about 90 % opacity, round caps, a hand wobble (a quadratic curve with 5-14 px of jitter), and a lighter 3.5 px core line in blue ink. Hatching outside a limit: 4.5 px grey ticks 46 × 34 px every 44 px, starting 30 px off the line. Dimension lines end in open 50 × 26 px arrowheads. - **Marker lettering:** each glyph its own span with a fixed seeded tilt (±3°) and baseline jitter (±3.5 % of its size), revealed left to right by a clip, one glyph every 0.07-0.1 s. - **Prints (z ≈ 10):** photo-real cut-outs painted once on a canvas (0.6×), with a light gradient from the window and a small grain pattern laid over the object only, then shown as an ``. Shadow: a soft rounded block offset 16 × 24 px, wide while the print is still in the air. - **Props:** glossy magnets (radial gradient with a specular dot, a soft offset shadow, no blur filter), magnetic tags and printed cards in `--latar-2` with a thin edge and a soft shadow, a sticky note, a stamp with a double rounded frame, a pale wash and a pitted impression (paper dots punched through the ink). - **Screen layers:** a diagonal reflection band that slides against the camera, a lens vignette, and the subtitle strip. Nothing else is in screen space. ## 3. Colour logic - `--latar` is the enamel; `--latar-2` is the window light on it, the tags, cards and the subtitle strip. The room wall around the frame mixes `--latar` toward a fixed warm shadow. - `--utama-di-latar` is the blue marker: limits, dimension lines and their arrowheads, the subtitle tick. On a pale brand it falls back to `--teks`, which reads as graphite measurement. - `--teks` is graphite: lettering, counts, the counting rail; magnets are `--teks` mixed toward black, so on a dark board they turn pale and still read. `--teks-redup` (mixed into the background) is the drafting grey: hatching and the dashed footprint of a rejected size. - `--aksen-di-latar` is the red verdict: the stamp's frame, words and pits wash, and the rule written after it with its underline. At most three red marks in a frame; never red on a red object. - `--utama` fills the contact pill on the closing card with `--teks-di-utama`; the tray's markers are `--utama`, `--aksen` and the magnet colour. - Fixed in every brand: the warm shadow (#2a2620), the reflection white, the aluminium greys, the sticky note and its ink, and the photograph's own colours (full colour belongs to the photograph only). ## 4. Type - `--font-judul` carries printed things: tags (800, 46 px, tracking 0.06 em, one to three words in capitals), the card's name (800, 66 px), the stamp (800, forced to the frame's width with `textLength` so a wider brand face still fits). Default Inter 800; Oswald 700 or Space Grotesk 700 suit it too. - `--font-isi` carries the subtitle strip (600, 34 px on top; 400, 22 px below in `--teks-redup`) and card body text (46 px). Default Inter 400/600. - The board's handwriting is a look token, `--font-spidol`: Patrick Hand at 150 px for measurements and counts, 190 px for the verdict rule (with a 3 px stroke for a fatter red marker). A brand does not replace it. - At the final whole-board frame (scale about 0.44), anything meant to be read must be at least 46 board px (20 px on screen); the subtitle strip carries the contact in readable size. ## 5. Motion quality - **Camera:** overlapping moves whose speed follows u^a (1−u)^b, so speed and acceleration never jump: a = 2, b = 3 for ordinary moves (0.5-1.0 s), a = 2.5, b = 4 for the long pull-back (1.45 s, a slow settle). Between moves a linear creep (scale +3-6 % over 2-3 s). A hand-held breath of at most 2.5 px, faded to zero 0.5 s before the final hold. - **Ink:** a dimension line draws in 0.3-0.5 s (`power3.out` when it whips past a limit), its far arrowhead taps on the frame it arrives; lettering starts 0.1-0.2 s after its line. - **Prints:** lowered from the camera side in 0.42 s (`power2.in`): scale 1.22 → 1, y −60 → 0, shadow 90 × 120 px → 16 × 24 px; a 1.2 % bounce (0.09 s each way). Magnets clack on 0.15 s later (scale 1.9 → 1 in 0.14 s, then a 0.05 s squash); lifting a print pops its magnets toward the lens (0.16 s) and raises it (scale 1.12, 0.32 s). - **Counting:** magnets clack on in rhythm, 0.2 s apart (the source film used about 0.35 s). - **Tags:** appear with their magnet and swing in on `elastic.out(1, 0.3)` from ±18-22° over 1.4 s. - **Stamp:** 0.09 s fall (`power4.in`, scale 1.3 → 1), a 1.5 % squash, the print beneath jolts 10 px, the camera shakes 8 px decaying over 0.4 s. Landings shake 2-2.5 px. - **Erase:** blur 3 px and opacity to 12 % over 0.3 s; the rejected size stays as a dashed footprint at 55 %. - **Subtitles:** cues fade in 0.15 s and out 0.12 s, at least 2.8 s each. - Never: dissolves between scenes, scale-pops on text, bouncy UI easing, text fading in by itself. The last 2 s are completely still. ## 6. Camera grammar | Move | What it expresses | Can serve | | --- | --- | --- | | Ride a line: start close on the arriving arrowhead, ease back until both limits show (2.3 s, scale 1.45 → 1.12) | measuring; "how far does it go?" | a width, a distance, a deadline on a timeline | | Travel sideways to the next drawing (1 s) and creep with the action | the same wall, the next fact | a count, a second option, the next step | | Pull back and sideways to the judgement frame: the whole item, its limit and room for the verdict (scale ≈ 0.76) | a test the viewer can check | pass / fail against a size, a budget against a cap | | Slow push-in with a Dutch tilt to −1.5° (3 s, +6 % scale) | tension before the verdict | a collision, an overrun, a failing test | | Shake on impact (8 px, 0.4 s) | the decision lands | a stamp, a rejection, a record | | Long pull-back to the whole board (1.45 s to scale ≈ 0.44, frame and tray in view) | everything at once, as a poster | the ending, a summary, the call to action | Framing: off-centre and cropped, a readable subject in the first frame, the first strong action within 0.5 s. Before the reveal, never the reveal zone and never both edges of the board. ## 7. Native moves - **Ride the dimension line.** A limit drawn as a real length, the camera riding the pen until both ends show and the number is written. *Fits content like:* the width of an alley a food cart must enter; the gap between two shelves in a shop; a creator measuring how far a phone drops in a test; the days left before a class's exam drawn as one long line. - **Magnets as countable things.** Units clack onto a graphite rail in rhythm, a tag says what one magnet is worth. *Fits content like:* houses in a street that have no shop yet; orders per day before and after a new menu; subscribers per month on a channel; votes in a class election. - **The print lands on the limit.** A photograph of the real thing is lowered onto the drawing and pinned; its own dimension line overshoots the limit. *Fits content like:* a standard cart wider than the alley; a sofa against a doorway; a suitcase against a cabin-bag frame; a delivery van in front of a low gate in a short story. - **The stamp.** A pitted verdict lands with a thud, a jolt and a camera shake, held at least 1.5 s in the judgement frame. *Fits content like:* "TIDAK MUAT"; a failed quality check at a workshop; a rejected thumbnail on a creator's board; a teacher marking the wrong method. - **Erase to a ghost, then the answer.** The rejected print is lifted off, its ink blurred to a ghost and its footprint left dashed; the answer lands in the same place and fits. *Fits content like:* the slim cart over the outline of the old one; this year's plan over last year's; a revised lesson plan over the first draft; the second attempt in a short story. - **The rule in red, then the whole wall.** After the verdict the new rule is written in red and underlined, and the camera pulls back to the whole board with the contact card pinned. *Fits content like:* "Maks. 90 cm" beside the workshop's card; a shop's opening rule; a channel's upload rule; the moral of a story. ## 8. Pitfalls - **Text glimpsed in passing.** Write where the camera rests; hold each number at least 1.5 s in frame. Lettering written during a camera move is read only after the move settles. - **Seeing the wall too early.** Keep later scenes' zones empty until their beat; the reveal zone (card, red rule, note) appears only at the end. - **A sparse or tiny final wall.** Size the poster so that readable words are at least 46 board px at the final scale; fill corners with quiet secondary items (a measurement card, a sticky note). - **Photos that don't belong together.** One grade, one light direction, one viewpoint (all from above here); never lettering or logos inside a photograph. - **Performance.** The whole board repaints when the camera moves, so keep it lean: textures and photographs painted once into canvases and turned into images (the enamel at quarter size), no blur filters on large or moving things, shadows as static box-shadows or gradients that only move, and no will-change on the board (a 4000 px composited layer is slower in the preview than repainting). - **Dash animation.** the timeline rounds pixel values, so give drawn paths `pathLength="1000"` and a gap longer than the dash (`1000 1200`), or a round cap leaves a dot at the end before the line draws. - **Brand colours.** Measurement must stay on `--utama-di-latar` and the verdict on `--aksen-di-latar`, never the raw tokens, so a pale yellow brand still draws readable lines; magnets and hatching are mixed from `--teks`, so a dark board keeps them visible. ## Measured from the references The source film is 12 s at 24 fps: measuring the limit 0-3.5 s (the line draws in about 0.6 s, the number follows), the first instinct built from seven magnets 3.5-7 s (one clack every 0.35 s), the real thing arriving and the stamp 7-9 s, the judgement frame held about 2.5 s, then the new rule in red and the start of the pull-back at 11 s. Blue lines are about 1 % of the frame height thick, lettering caps about 11 % of it, the subtitle strip sits 4-6 % above the bottom edge.

# Briefing board: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2.4, medium 3.2, long 4.2.

## hook

- en: close on a blue dimension line as it reaches its limit; the camera eases back while the number is written glyph by glyph
- id: dekat di garis ukur biru yang tiba di batasnya; kamera mundur pelan sambil angkanya ditulis huruf demi huruf

## problem

- en: the photo is lowered onto its limit and pinned; its dimension overshoots, a red stamp lands with a thud and a shake
- id: foto benda diturunkan ke batasnya dan dipaku magnet; garis ukurnya kebablasan, cap merah jatuh dengan hentakan

## fact

- en: the camera rides a line to a magnetic tag swinging beside a drawn limit; graphite lettering names the fact
- id: kamera menyusuri garis ke label magnet yang berayun di samping batas; tulisan spidol grafit menyebut faktanya

## step

- en: each step is a magnet clacking onto a graphite rail with a short tag; the camera slides along with them
- id: tiap langkah satu magnet yang menempel di rel grafit dengan label pendek; kamera ikut bergeser

## compare

- en: two photos against the same limit, each with its dimension line; the loser is erased to a ghost under the winner
- id: dua foto diuji di batas yang sama, masing-masing dengan garis ukur; yang kalah dihapus jadi bayangan

## number

- en: magnets clack onto a rail in rhythm, 0.2 s apart; a swinging tag says what one magnet is worth
- id: magnet menempel berirama di rel, tiap 0,2 detik; label berayun menyebut nilai satu magnet

## proof

- en: a printed measurement card pinned by a magnet; the camera rests on it while a blue line measures beside it
- id: kartu catatan ukur dipaku magnet; kamera berhenti di situ sementara garis biru mengukur di sebelahnya

## offer

- en: the answer's photo lands inside the limit and fits, its blue dimension drawn; the rule is written in red, underlined
- id: foto jawaban mendarat di dalam batas dan pas, garis ukurnya digambar; aturannya ditulis merah, digarisbawahi

## cta

- en: long pull-back to the whole board: the card with name and contact pinned by two magnets, held 2 s
- id: kamera mundur jauh ke seluruh papan: kartu nama dan kontak dipaku dua magnet, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the opening limit, now answered, circled in red; the camera pulls back to the whole board and holds 2 s
- id: batas di awal kini terjawab dan dilingkari merah; kamera mundur ke seluruh papan lalu diam 2 detik

      /* Token brand (recipes/README.md): brand mengganti dua belas nilai pertama. */
      :root {
        --latar: #ebe6dc; --latar-2: #f8f6f1; --utama: #2c49b0; --aksen: #c8433a;
        --teks: #34322d; --teks-redup: #757067; --teks-di-utama: #ffffff; --teks-di-aksen: #ffffff;
        --utama-di-latar: #2c49b0; --aksen-di-latar: #c8433a;
        --font-judul: "Inter", "Noto Sans", sans-serif; --font-isi: "Inter", "Noto Sans", sans-serif;
        /* Tulisan spidol adalah bahan papan, bukan huruf brand. */
        --font-spidol: "Patrick Hand", "Noto Sans", sans-serif;
        /* Tetap di semua brand: bayangan, kilap, rangka aluminium, kertas tempel, warna foto gerobak. */
        --bayang: #2a2620; --kilap: #ffffff; --alu: #c9c6bf; --alu-gelap: #8e8b84; --catatan: #f1e29a; --tinta: #2c2a26;

        /* Dicampur dari token supaya papan ikut brand. */
        --magnet: color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks) 88%, black);
        --arsir: color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks-redup) 80%, var(--latar));
        --dinding: color-mix(in oklab, var(--latar) 62%, var(--bayang));
        --cap: color-mix(in oklab, var(--aksen) 8%, var(--latar-2));
        --bayang-lunak: color-mix(in oklab, var(--bayang) 24%, transparent);
      }
      * { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }
      html, body { width: 1920px; height: 1080px; overflow: hidden; background: var(--dinding); }
      #root { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: var(--dinding); color: var(--teks); font-family: var(--font-isi); }
      /* Dunia dalam piksel papan (3900 × 2200); kamera hanya mengubah transform #dunia. */
      #dunia, .abs, .scene, .ink, .mag, .print, .tag, .kartu, .cap, .spidol { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; }
      #dunia { transform-origin: 0 0; }
      #rangka { left: -34px; top: -34px; width: 3968px; height: 2268px; border-radius: 16px; background: linear-gradient(165deg, var(--alu), var(--alu-gelap));
        box-shadow: 0 40px 90px color-mix(in oklab, var(--bayang) 45%, transparent); }
      #papan, #email { width: 3900px; height: 2200px; overflow: hidden; }
      #baki { left: 300px; top: 2214px; width: 3300px; height: 64px; border-radius: 8px; background: linear-gradient(var(--alu), var(--alu-gelap)); }
      #baki i { position: absolute; top: -14px; width: 300px; height: 34px; border-radius: 17px; }
      .ink { overflow: visible; }
      .ink path, .ink rect { fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }
      .biru { stroke: var(--utama-di-latar); stroke-width: 11; opacity: 0.92; }
      .inti { stroke: color-mix(in oklab, var(--utama-di-latar) 55%, var(--latar)); stroke-width: 3.5; opacity: 0.55; }
      .grafit { stroke: var(--teks); stroke-width: 10; opacity: 0.9; }
      .arsir { stroke: var(--arsir); stroke-width: 4.5; }
      .merah { stroke: var(--aksen-di-latar); stroke-width: 12; opacity: 0.9; }
      .jejak { stroke: var(--arsir); stroke-width: 6; stroke-dasharray: 26 20; }
      .spidol { font-family: var(--font-spidol); line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--teks); }
      .spidol i { display: inline-block; font-style: normal; }
      .spidol.vonis { color: var(--aksen-di-latar); -webkit-text-stroke: 3px var(--aksen-di-latar); }
      /* Magnet dan bayangan dari gradasi, tanpa blur. */
      .mag > div { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; }
      .mag .sh { inset: -18%; background: radial-gradient(closest-side, color-mix(in oklab, var(--bayang) 55%, transparent), transparent); }
      .mag .b { background: radial-gradient(circle at 36% 30%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--magnet), white 70%) 0, color-mix(in oklab, var(--magnet), white 14%) 20%, var(--magnet) 50%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--magnet), black 50%) 100%); }
      /* Foto: bayangan satu jendela (box-shadow diam, hanya digeser). */
      .print .sh { position: absolute; inset: 2% 6% 16%; border-radius: 60px; background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--bayang) 30%, transparent);
        box-shadow: 0 0 60px 34px color-mix(in oklab, var(--bayang) 26%, transparent); }
      .print .ph { position: absolute; inset: 0; }
      .tag, .kartu { background: var(--latar-2); color: var(--teks); border: 2px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks) 14%, transparent); box-shadow: 8px 12px 22px var(--bayang-lunak); }
      .tag { padding: 18px 34px 14px; border-radius: 10px; font: 800 46px var(--font-judul); letter-spacing: 0.06em; white-space: nowrap; transform-origin: 50% 0; }
      .tag .mag { left: 50%; top: -46px; margin-left: -30px; }
      .kartu { border-radius: 8px; padding: 46px 56px; }
      .kartu b { display: block; font: 800 66px/1.1 var(--font-judul); }
      .kartu p { font-size: 46px; line-height: 1.3; color: var(--teks-redup); margin-top: 14px; }
      .pil { display: inline-block; margin-top: 26px; padding: 12px 34px; border-radius: 40px; background: var(--utama); color: var(--teks-di-utama); font-weight: 600; font-size: 50px; }

      .cap-garis { fill: none; stroke: var(--aksen-di-latar); stroke-width: 4; }

      .strip small { display: block; font-size: 22px; line-height: 1.3; color: var(--teks-redup); }
